claims.text: The target materials are pristine, chemically disordered, single-phase HEAs that may have equiatomic BCC or FCC structures.
An integrated ML-potential, CALPHAD, and MD/Monte Carlo framework will determine HEA melting temperatures accurately and efficiently.
The integrated framework will accurately determine HEA fusion enthalpy and entropy.
The integrated framework will accurately determine volume changes at melting in HEAs.
The integrated framework will determine key liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across single-phase HEAs.
Short-range chemical order and associated local structural changes influence atomic vibrations or displacements in HEAs.
Local lattice distortions and short-range chemical order influence the free-energy landscape near melting.
ML-trained interatomic potentials capture subtle multicomponent interactions and local lattice distortions in HEAs.
Integrating CALPHAD ensures that atomistic predictions remain consistent with macroscopic thermodynamics.
Combining ML potentials, CALPHAD, and MD/Monte Carlo facilitates efficient sampling of atomic configurations near melting.
Atomic displacements, energy fluctuations, and phase-transition dynamics can be analyzed to extract melting temperature, fusion properties, volume changes, and liquid properties.
Predicted melting temperatures and fusion thermodynamic properties will be within approximately 5–10% of experimental values.
The approach will quantitatively describe liquid-phase behavior over a wide compositional range of single-phase HEAs.
Traditional ab initio or classical MD methods without ML enhancement or CALPHAD integration have limited configurational sampling.
Traditional ab initio or classical MD methods have higher computational cost and yield less accurate or less efficient predictions than the proposed framework.
The approach is most applicable to moderately complex, single-phase HEAs.
HEAs exhibiting strong phase separation, ordering, or multiphase behavior may fall outside the reliable prediction range.
Prediction errors depend on the quality of the ML potential and the completeness of available CALPHAD data.
